Part One
of the book
Shams al-Maʿārif
al-Kubrā
and Laṭāʾif al-ʿAwārif
by Shaykh Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī al-Būnī; may Allah sanctify his spirit; he died in the year 622 AH.
It is stated in Kashf al-Ẓunūn: The purpose of this book is to make known through it the nobility of the Names of Allah, exalted is He, and what has been deposited
in their sea of various wisdom-jewels; and how to work with the Names and invocations, and what follows them,
of the letters of the sūrahs and verses, so that through them one may reach the Divine Presence without toil and reach through them
the desires of this world without hardship. End quote.
❖ And following it ❖
The Epistle of the Balance of Justice on the Purposes of the Rules of Sand ❖ the Epistle of the Openings of Desires on the Particular Properties of
the Planets' Times ❖ the Epistle of the Flowers of the Meadows on the Signs of the Zodiac ❖ the Epistle of the Subtleties of Indication
on the Special Properties of the Wandering Planets ❖ authored by the eminent scholar, Sayyid ʿAbd al-Qādir al-Ḥusaynī al-Adhamī
❖ May Allah benefit the Muslims through his knowledge. Amen.
❖ Notice ❖
Since the book Shams al-Maʿārif, owing to the people's great need for it, has been printed many times (in Egypt and India), and the Egyptian printing presses took care to correct it,
yet it was not free from errors and distortions because correct copies were unavailable.
This time it has been printed after collation with copies from “Egypt and India” and another copy in the handwriting of Hajj Mirza Husayn,
with careful correction by a committee of eminent Egyptian scholars; it was corrected again by the great scholar Shaykh
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jazīrī. Thus, praise be to Allah, this edition has become one of the finest copies in both printing and correction.
Printed at the press of
Muṣṭafā al-Bābī al-Ḥalabī and his sons in Egypt

karya Syekh Ahmad bin Ali al-Buni; semoga Allah menyucikan rohnya; ia wafat pada tahun 622 H.
Disebutkan dalam Kasyf al-Zunun: Tujuan kitab ini adalah agar melalui kitab ini dapat diketahui kemuliaan Nama-Nama Allah, Yang Mahatinggi, serta apa yang telah disimpan
dalam "lautan" nama-nama itu berupa berbagai permata hikmah; juga bagaimana menggunakan nama-nama dan doa-doa, beserta hal-hal yang mengikutinya,
berupa huruf-huruf surah dan ayat, agar dengannya seseorang dapat mencapai Hadirat Ilahi tanpa kelelahan dan mencapai melaluinya
keinginan-keinginan duniawi tanpa kesusahan. Selesai kutipan.
❖ Dan menyusulnya ❖
Risalah Timbangan Keadilan tentang Tujuan Hukum-Hukum Raml ❖ Risalah Pembuka Keinginan tentang Kekhususan
Waktu-Waktu Planet ❖ Risalah Bunga-Bunga Padang tentang Petunjuk Zodiak ❖ Risalah Latha'if al-Isyarah
mengenai Kekhususan Planet-Planet yang Berjalan ❖ karya ulama terkemuka, Sayyid Abd al-Qadir al-Husayni al-Adhami
❖ Semoga Allah memberi manfaat kepada kaum Muslimin melalui ilmunya. Amin.
❖ Peringatan ❖
Karena kitab Syams al-Ma'arif, akibat besarnya kebutuhan masyarakat terhadapnya, telah dicetak berkali-kali (di Mesir dan India), dan percetakan-percetakan Mesir telah berupaya mengoreksinya,
namun kitab ini tidak luput dari kesalahan dan penyimpangan karena tidak adanya naskah-naskah yang benar.
Kali ini kitab ini dicetak setelah dibandingkan dengan naskah-naskah "Mesir dan India" serta satu naskah lain yang ditulis tangan oleh Haji Mirza Husain,
dengan ketelitian dalam koreksi oleh sebuah komite yang terdiri atas para ulama terkemuka Mesir; kitab ini dikoreksi kembali oleh ulama besar, Syekh
Abd al-Rahman al-Jaziri. Dengan demikian, alhamdulillah, edisi ini menjadi salah satu salinan terbaik dalam hal pencetakan dan koreksi.
Dicetak di percetakan
Mustafa al-Babi al-Halabi dan putra-putranya di Mesir

And to Allah belong the Most Beautiful Names, so call upon Him by them.

In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

A testimony of pre-eternity; from the light of this testimony the chosen ones drew knowledge. Understand this, and the order that appeared in the two testimonies
connected with the noble angels and those endowed with knowledge. This is the testimony of eternity, for within them lies the secret of these two testimonies: the witness
of the two realms and what they deposited through the secret of connection with revelatory unveilings; and for every form there is a path to all wisdoms.

I ask Allah, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, to make it sincere and an accepted offering before my private supplication, and to let its spirit of comfort accompany me
in my movements and my dwelling; to make the path clear to me and to you; and to bestow upon us and upon you the lights of realization. Indeed, this mercy-filled flash
and the radiant, illuminating suns are the paths of the knowers, the way of the truthful, and the broad road of the righteous,
leading to the holy presence of the Lord of the worlds, Lord of lords, Opener of causes, and Lifter of the veil, which He originated without a model,
transcendent above forms, everlasting, never ceasing to be described by the attributes of beauty, eternally existent in pre-eternity, raising the higher realms
by His determination and wisdom, and spreading the lower realms by His power and will. There is no god but Him, the Great, the Most High,
veiled by the veils of light, hidden from all secrets, concealed from the enclosures of vision; yet He perceives all vision through His inward aspect, by His Essence, in His pre-eternity.
He became manifest through His attributes in His eternity, revealed Himself through His instruments in His sempiternity, and manifested through His acts in His eternity.
He is the First in pre-eternity, the Last in eternity, and the Manifest in sempiternity. Exalted is He above
substances and accidents, bodies and parts, and being subject to purposes. Directions and regions cannot contain Him;
the succession of cycles does not follow Him, and the passing of night and day does not annihilate Him. I praise Him,
glorified and exalted is He. Everything with Him is measured. He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Great, the Most High. And I bear witness that there is no god but
Allah alone, without partner. It is a testimony that accompanies souls with steadfast confirmation in the barzakh realms. And I bear witness to you: His creation has encompassed it,
living and dead. He sees the dead and their provisions, knows what has passed and what is to come, and revives the dead
after they have become remains. And I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, the sun of the religious community and the deliverer of the servants from polytheism
and humiliation.

Yang tersembunyi di balik tabir-tabir cahaya, terlindung dari seluruh rahasia, tersembunyi dari tirai-tirai penglihatan; namun Dia menangkap segala penglihatan dengan batin-Nya, dengan Zat-Nya, dalam keazalian-Nya.
Dia menampakkan diri melalui sifat-sifat-Nya dalam keabadian-Nya, menyatakan diri melalui sarana-sarana-Nya dalam kekekalan-Nya, dan menampakkan diri melalui perbuatan-perbuatan-Nya dalam keabadian-Nya.
Dialah Yang Awal dalam keazalian, Yang Akhir dalam keabadian, dan Yang Zahir dalam kekekalan. Mahasuci Dia dari
substansi dan aksiden, tubuh dan bagian-bagian, serta dari tunduk pada tujuan-tujuan. Arah dan penjuru tidak dapat meliputi-Nya;
pergantian siklus tidak mengikuti-Nya, dan berlalunya malam dan siang tidak membinasakan-Nya. Aku memuji-Nya,
Mahasuci dan Mahatinggi Dia. Segala sesuatu di sisi-Nya berada dalam ukuran. Dia Maha Mengetahui yang gaib dan yang nyata, Yang Maha Besar, Yang Mahatinggi. Dan aku bersaksi bahwa tiada tuhan selain
Allah semata, tiada sekutu bagi-Nya. Kesaksian itu menyertai ruh-ruh dengan peneguhan di alam-alam barzakh. Dan aku bersaksi kepada kalian: makhluk-Nya telah meliputinya,
baik yang hidup maupun yang mati. Dia melihat orang-orang mati dan rezeki-rezeki, mengetahui apa yang telah berlalu dan apa yang akan datang, serta menghidupkan orang-orang mati
setelah mereka menjadi sisa-sisa jasad. Dan aku bersaksi bahwa Muhammad adalah hamba dan Rasul-Nya, matahari umat beragama dan penyelamat para hamba dari kesyirikan
dan kehinaan.

Among them is what appears together with them, and they are fourteen letters, as you see: alif, bāʾ, jīm, ḥāʾ, kāf, mīm, ʿayn, ghayn, fāʾ, qāf, hāʾ, wāw, and yāʾ. The first of the letters is alif, followed by letters such as acts of obedience, definiteness forms, and rāʾs, all belonging to the side of alif and what follows it. When an observer considers the letters, he finds them corresponding within the soul before they exist in physical form, so understand. Alif among the letters is the one among the numbers, and numbers are a subtle spiritual power. Reliance upon it is therefore among the secrets of utterances, just as letters are among the secrets of actions. Numbers in the human world have secrets and benefits that He, exalted is His power, has arranged just as letters are arranged: secrets of benefit such as supplication, incantation, and whatever else whose effect becomes manifest to the world through various names. (And know)
that letters have no time that confines them; rather, they act through spiritual discipline and special properties for whomever He wills, while numbers act through talismans and are connected to higher-world correspondences. (As for the letter dāl,) it has the numerical value four. Whoever constructs a figure should multiply 4 by 4 and place within it the correspondence of Monday—the day the Prophet was born, the day he was commissioned, and the day he died—under the moon's exaltation at three degrees of Taurus, free from malefic influences. Let the hour belong to the moon, and write it after complete purification and two cycles of prayer, reciting Āyat al-Kursī and al-Ikhlāṣ one hundred times, on pure parchment. Whoever carries this wafq with him will have memorization and understanding made easy for him by God, and his rank will be magnified before the upper and lower worlds alike. If a prisoner carries it, he will be freed by God's permission. Whoever carries it on a banner will defeat the enemies among the unbelievers and aggressors. Whoever carries it and disputes with someone through it will overcome and subdue him. Its numerical arrangement is 4 by 4, and its form is made by multiplying 4 by 4. It belongs to the four elements—fire, air, earth, and water—and to the four humors: yellow bile, phlegm, blood, and black bile. These are four, not a quarter; thus it has the power of the temperaments and their balance. This noble letter appears especially in His name al-Dāʾim, and in His name al-Wadūd. Nothing precedes dāl in al-Dāʾim, and for that reason the two noble and generous names are Aḥmad and Muḥammad. This indicates that permanence is the final end of its beginning: it follows dāl in the word for permanence. It was placed first in His name al-Dāʾim because He possesses permanence at both beginning and end, and He granted His servants a share in enduring existence after annihilation in the Hereafter. This letter belongs to the Throne because its existence does not change: it is the first world of originated things, the first world, and the place to which spirits ascend. In it are the degrees of intellects and the lights of mercy. Some people who know God have disclosed this in connection with the portion allotted to Ḥārithah, may God be pleased with him, when the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, asked him, “How did you awake, O Ḥārithah?”
Ḥārithah replied, “O Messenger of God, I awoke a true believer.” The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, asked, “What is the reality of your faith?”
Ḥārithah replied, “I awoke having presented myself to the world; its stones and gold, its living and dead, its rich and poor, had become equal to me. It was as though I were looking upon the Throne of the Merciful unveiled, while people were being driven to the reckoning, to Paradise, and to the Fire.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him, “You have understood, so remain steadfast.” The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, also said concerning spirits: “When they appear in a state of purity from ablution, they remain prostrating beneath the Throne.” (The letter dāl) has among its secrets permanence and abiding existence. Al-shaqq is a subtlety between love and wudd; its dwelling is shaghaf, and the most beloved inward aspect of passion dwells in the fuʾād, because the heart has three cavities. The locus of Islam and the meanings of the letters there is difficult to explain; it is also the locus of the speaking faculty in the human being that governs the meanings of the will issuing from the soul. The second cavity is in the middle of the heart. It is the place of reflection and remembrance, a radiant light, the place of tranquility, and the place of the imagination in what the spirit casts into it. The third cavity is at its far end; it is the most delicate and subtle of them. It is called the fuʾād, and it is the place of faith, intellect, light, agency, secrets, the balance of the intellect, the subtleties of wisdom, and the life of nature through subtle heat. Therefore, this fuʾād has a luminous eye through which it perceives the realities of the malakūt, the secrets of the higher worlds, particulars and universals, and the measures of realities. It is the place of gifted lights and the secrets of the higher worlds. That is the insight by which it sees, concerning which God says: “It is not the eyes that are blind, but the hearts within the chests.”
The middle cavity, which is the place of passionate love, has a luminous eye through which the object of seeking is perceived. From it arise earnestness in seeking and longing for the sought thing. Because of its subtlety, it attaches more quickly to persons. Through it the world of visible dominion and all that it contains of God's creation is unveiled, and through it appreciation of beautiful things takes place. Then the first cavity has a luminous eye through which one looks upon the secrets of sensory things, the states of composite beings, and the realities of letters and their secrets, as well as the immense things God has deposited in them: the secrets of the Divine Names and the realities of their meanings. Through it, this becomes a gift to God's servants and a means of glorifying God by knowing Him through it and through what He has bestowed upon it by unveiling the secrets of sensory things. These are all the insights of the hearts, although people differ in the ways matters differ.
It was mentioned earlier, in the discussion of the times of insights and the subtleties of inner secrets, that the spirits of revelation in the Book of God are three: the Spirit of the Trustworthy One, the Spirit of Holiness, and the Spirit of the Command. The Spirit of the Trustworthy One indicates the first cavity because it is the intermediary between utterance and the tongue. It is the first rank of revelation in its descent, each according to what God has allotted to it of inspiration and revelation upon the hearts. After it comes the Spirit of Holiness, which consists of the lights of what reaches the second rank of the heart from the Preserved Tablet. (Di antara khasiatnya) untuk kecintaan: tulislah “kābāynāh” pada waktu yang baik. Apply this by analogy to whatever works and actions suit it; your work will succeed, and God grants success to what is right. If you desire works of corruption, do as we first described: hatred, destruction, ruin, and whatever resembles them. Apply the same analogy and act, and you will attain the intended result. God speaks the truth, and He guides the way.

This is the invocation of the letter alif with which you invoke the preceding number:

“Glory be to You; there is no god but You, O Lord of everything, its Inheritor, and the earth.”

(The second mansion,) the mansion of al-Buṭayn, belongs to the letter bāʾ. When the moon descends into it, a spiritual force descends from it by God's command, suitable for anger and for what was mentioned earlier. Medicine is drunk in it, and the nobles, worldly people, and kings of the earth become active in it, because it is the second face of Aries and the face of the Sun. Its exaltation is there at nineteen degrees of it, on the fourth day of April. The Sun is fortunate, although hot and dry. Its fortune and exaltation in this face make it suitable for working for acceptance, approaching kings, and whatever is sought from them, for needs are fulfilled. Work for affection, acceptance, and attracting hearts; bring them forth through it. It is also suitable for the practice of the wisdom-crafts, golden elixirs, and their preparation.

(The third mansion,) the mansion of al-Thurayyā, has the letter jīm. When the moon descends into it, a spiritual force descends from it compounded of heat, moisture, and cold. It has a moderate fortune, is good for travel, for associating with nobles, for approaching the great ones, the lords of the world, and people of the pen, because al-Thurayyā is a dense gathering of stars.

Beramallah untuk kasih sayang, penerimaan, dan penarikan hati; wujudkanlah hal-hal itu dengannya. Ia juga sesuai untuk pembuatan kerajinan hikmah, eliksir emas, dan pengolahannya.

(Manzilah ketiga,) manzilah al-Thurayyā, memiliki huruf jīm. Apabila bulan turun padanya, turun darinya suatu kekuatan ruhani yang bercampur antara panas, kelembapan, dan dingin. Ia memiliki keberuntungan sedang, baik untuk perjalanan, bergaul dengan para bangsawan, mendatangi para pembesar, para penguasa dunia, dan para ahli pena, karena al-Thurayyā merupakan kumpulan bintang yang sangat banyak.
